site.name: lattice
site.summary: lattice-clone Fictional hosted columnar / relational database "Lattice DB" marketing site, centered on the two-dimensional matrix on the pricing page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Short landing: technical paragraph + SQL code example + 3 features + CTA | | `pricing.html` | Main page: 6 rows (seats) × 6 columns (data volume) two-dimensional matrix; clicking a cell highlights the row and column and updates the right-side sticky quote card (with a "How this is calculated" expansion); 9 add-on checkboxes (percentage or flat add-on); bottom final monthly-fee breakdown card; 4-tier explainer (clicking a cell auto-highlights the corresponding tier); 15-row feature comparison; 8-question FAQ; footer | | `styles.css` | Brand color #6D28D9 purple; IBM Plex Sans + Mono; responsive |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lattice system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Lattice DB pricing page features a highly functional and reactive cost calculator on desktop, but suffers from significant layout and usability issues on mobile viewports. Key challenges include pervasive horizontal overflow caused by wide tables, unacceptably small tap targets for checkboxes, and overlapping text near the FAQ section. Additionally, a logical flaw in the calculator misleads users by summing flat-fee add-ons against a $0 base when a custom 'Contact us' tier is selected.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lattice system, prioritizing the primary pricing flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the landing page to verify navigation and basic layout, before dedicating the majority of effort to the complex pricing page. The pricing page evaluation will focus on the interactive 2D matrix, state updates in the sticky quote card, tier highlighting, and the add-on calculator logic. Finally, the run will heavily evaluate how this large matrix and sticky layout perform on a mobile viewport.
assumptions: Clicking a `td` cell in the pricing matrix triggers JavaScript state changes on the page.
The sticky quote card and bottom fee breakdown update dynamically based on cell selection and add-on checkbox states.
The 'How this is calculated' section is an expandable element (accordion/details).
risk_hotspots: Responsiveness and usability of the 6x6 pricing matrix on mobile.
Behavior of the sticky quote card overlapping or breaking layout on smaller screens.
Accuracy of the dynamic calculations when combining flat-fee and percentage-based add-ons.
Navigation links identified as having small tap targets.

phases.title: Landing Page & Navigation
phases.objective: Verify the basic structure, branding, and navigation paths from the landing page.
key_checks: Check global header links and note the small tap targets reported in the prescan.
Ensure the 'See pricing' CTA properly routes to the pricing page.
exit_criteria: Navigated successfully to pricing.html via CTA.

phases.title: Pricing Matrix Interaction (Desktop)
phases.objective: Validate the core interactive 2D matrix for seat/data volume selection.
key_checks: Click multiple cells (e.g., $169, $659, Contact us) and verify that row/column highlighting updates.
Verify that the 'SELECTED CELL' in the quote card updates with the correct dollar amount and tier.
Verify that clicking a cell correctly auto-highlights the corresponding tier in the 4-tier explainer section.
exit_criteria: Multiple distinct cells selected with confirmed state changes in the DOM/UI.

phases.title: Add-ons & Calculator Logic
phases.objective: Test the behavior of add-on checkboxes and the final fee breakdown.
key_checks: Expand the 'How we got this number' / 'How this is calculated' section.
Toggle a mix of flat-fee (e.g., +$400/mo) and percentage-based (+15%) add-ons.
Verify the bottom final monthly-fee breakdown card calculates the expected total.
exit_criteria: Add-ons toggled and calculator breakdown visually updated.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Stress Test
phases.objective: Evaluate the complex table and calculator on mobile.
key_checks: Attempt to scroll and interact with the 6x6 matrix (check for horizontal scrolling or layout breakage).
Observe the positioning of the sticky quote card—does it block the viewport?
exit_criteria: Matrix and calculator interactions completed and screenshotted under mobile constraints.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise matrix cell selection, tier highlighting, quote expansion, and all add-on types.
coverage_targets.mobile: Strictly evaluate the horizontal overflow of the pricing table and the usability of the sticky calculator on mobile.

notes: The prescan highlighted multiple 'small_tap_target' warnings on nav links. Note this in the final UX critique.
Be sure to click at least one 'Contact us' cell in the matrix to see how the calculator handles non-numeric states.

findings.user_goal: Compare pricing tiers and features easily on a mobile device.
findings.problem: The main pricing matrix, tier explainer cards, and feature matrix fail to adapt to narrow screens, causing persistent horizontal scrolling that cuts off content.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings report 'Page width 475px exceeds viewport 390px,' and trajectory chunks indicate the rightmost columns and side-by-side tier explainer cards force users to pan horizontally.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling on mobile is highly frustrating for users. It makes it difficult to read tabular data or understand tier structures, often increasing bounce rates.
findings.suggestion: Implement responsive wrappers for the tables (allowing localized horizontal scrolling within the table container) and stack the tier explainer cards vertically on small screens.

findings.user_goal: Select optional add-ons to estimate the total monthly cost on a phone.
findings.problem: The checkboxes for selecting add-ons, as well as navigation and footer links, have extremely small touch targets, making them difficult to tap accurately with a finger.
findings.evidence: Multiple layout warnings flag 13x13px sizes for inputs like 'Continuous cross-region backups +15%' and 26px bounding box heights for footer links.
findings.why_it_matters: Tiny tap targets lead to accidental clicks and user frustration, severely degrading the accessibility of the interactive pricing calculator on mobile devices.
findings.suggestion: Increase the physical size of the checkboxes and wrap the labels inside clickable `<label>` tags to expand the total hit area to at least the standard 44x44px recommendation.

findings.user_goal: Understand potential costs when requesting a custom quote for large enterprise deployments.
findings.problem: When a user selects a 'Contact us' cell and checks a flat-fee add-on, the calculator sets the base price to $0 and shows a total consisting only of the add-on cost.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes: 'When a Contact us base pricing tier is selected and a flat-fee add-on (e.g., HIPAA compliance pack +$400/mo) is checked, the FINAL ESTIMATED COST displays a total consisting only of the add-on amount (Total · $400/mo).'
findings.why_it_matters: Displaying a specific dollar total that omits a custom enterprise base price is highly misleading and sets inaccurate pricing expectations for high-value customers.
findings.suggestion: If the base tier is 'Contact us', override the Total display to explicitly state 'Contact us' or 'Custom pricing' rather than summing numerical add-ons onto a $0 base.

findings.user_goal: Read through the product feature comparisons and FAQ clearly.
findings.problem: On mobile viewports, text content from the bottom of the Feature Matrix overlaps the FAQ section header below it.
findings.evidence: Trajectory steps 55-60 mention 'broken layout text (e.g., 1 bday, 4h) floating above the FAQ heading. This appears to be overlapping content from the feature matrix above.'
findings.why_it_matters: Overlapping text looks unprofessional, diminishes brand trust, and can obscure important information, making the site feel broken.
findings.suggestion: Ensure proper margin spacing and overflow handling (e.g., `overflow: hidden` or `auto` on the table wrapper) between the feature matrix block and the FAQ section.
findings.source_hint: Feature matrix table container, FAQ section header

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site to book a demo, read documentation, or view customer stories.
findings.problem: Major interactive navigation links, including the primary 'Book demo' CTA, are non-functional stubs that merely append a hash (#) to the URL.
findings.evidence: Trajectory logs repeatedly report that clicking 'Book demo', 'Docs', 'Customers', and footer links like 'Security' fails to navigate anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: Users trying to learn more or commit to the product hit dead ends, entirely blocking conversion flows (like booking a demo).
findings.suggestion: Replace stub links with actual URLs pointing to the correct pages. If the pages are not built yet, consider hiding or disabling the links until they are ready.

findings.user_goal: Easily read the state of the highlighted pricing cell.
findings.problem: The text 'Contact us' inside the large selected cell quote card has unusually wide spacing, making it visually awkward.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes: 'The large Contact us typography in the Selected Cell card displays an unusually wide space between the words, appearing visually awkward.'
findings.why_it_matters: Poor typographic layout in a key visual focal point makes the design feel unpolished and reduces the perceived quality of the product.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the word-spacing, letter-spacing, or line-break behavior for the selected cell text specifically when it displays non-numeric text.
